title: Checkpoint: The American Revolution
objective: After this level you can explain how a tax dispute became a war for independence, and who gained and lost by it.
summary: A timeline from the Stamp Act (1765) to the Treaty of Paris (1783), then who gained and who lost by independence.

cards.headline: Chapter 3 finale: a quarrel over stamps became a new nation.
cards.body: Put the whole Revolution on one timeline. Then ask who won, and who lost.

events.label: The Stamp Act taxes colonial paper
The Treaty of Paris ends the war

cards.headline: Who gained, who lost
cards.body: Independence rested on a promise: governments get “their just powers from the consent of the governed.” Not everyone shared in it. About 60,000 to 100,000 Loyalists went into exile. Most Native nations that fought had sided with Britain to keep their lands, and the Six Nations, allies of both sides, got no provision in the peace.

cards.headline: Voices left out
cards.body: Thousands of enslaved people escaped to British lines, and Pennsylvania and Massachusetts began to end slavery, Pennsylvania only gradually. Abigail Adams asked the lawmakers to remember the ladies, and New Jersey let some women vote until 1807. The Revolution’s promise was bigger than its first results.

cards.headline: Chapter 3 complete

Why the Declaration’s promise of equality clashed with slavery, and who said so.
How Saratoga, the French alliance and Yorktown let an outmatched army win.

questions.prompt: Put these events of the Revolution in order, from earliest to latest.
items: The Stamp Act taxes colonial paper
The Treaty of Paris ends the war
questions.explanation: The Stamp Act came in 1765, the Boston Tea Party in 1773, Lexington and Concord in 1775, the Declaration in 1776, Yorktown in 1781, and the Treaty of Paris in 1783.

questions.prompt: What did the Treaty of Paris of 1783 provide for Britain’s Six Nations allies?

options.label: Their own seat in Congress
options.rationale: They got no provision at all.

options.label: Nothing: it made no provision for them
All the land east of the Mississippi
options.rationale: The treaty made no provision for them.

options.label: Payment for their losses in the war
options.rationale: They got no provision at all.

questions.explanation: Neither Britain nor the United States made any provision for their Six Nations allies.

questions.prompt: How did Parliament’s punishment of Boston in 1774 help lead to war in 1775?

options.label: It united the colonies, and Massachusetts armed
It made Boston pay for all the tea at once
It gave colonists their own seats in Parliament
It ended the colonial boycott of British goods
options.rationale: Congress called for a boycott instead.

questions.explanation: The Intolerable Acts brought the First Continental Congress, and Massachusetts armed its militia and minutemen.

questions.prompt: The 1776 pamphlet that called it absurd for an island to govern a continent was _____.

options.label: the Declaratory Act
options.rationale: That was an act of Parliament claiming power over the colonies.

questions.explanation: Thomas Paine’s Common Sense mocked a continent “perpetually governed by an island.”

questions.prompt: What did Abigail Adams, Prince Hall and Elizabeth Freeman each do with the Revolution’s ideas?

options.label: Argued publicly against independence from Britain
options.rationale: All three used the Revolution’s own ideas.

options.label: Applied its rights talk to people it left out
Fought in the siege of Yorktown in 1781

questions.explanation: Adams asked for women’s voice, Hall petitioned for Black freedom, and Freeman won hers in court.
